issues.title: Midnight timestamps in start/end parse as bare dates and expand to whole-day bounds.
issues.why: Both routes declare `start`/`end` as `date | datetime | None`. Under the locked pydantic 2.12.5 / fastapi 0.136.1, I reproduced that `end=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` and `end=2026-06-01T00:00:00+05:00` both validate as `date(2026, 6, 1)`, while `...T00:00:01Z` stays a datetime. `resolve_window` then turns that date into `23:59:59.999999` UTC, so an explicit midnight end returns an extra day of rows, and an offset midnight loses its offset. This is new code in base..head and returns wrong data silently.

issues.title: Building and serializing a ceiling-sized response runs synchronously on the event loop.
issues.why: Only the DB reads go through `run_in_executor`. `CandlesResponse.build`/`TradesResponse.build` (up to 75,000 pydantic records) and `timeseries_response` run inline in the `async def`. Reviewers measured about 1.2 s for this, and the load test records a 34.8 MB candle body. The repo's python rule (.claude/rules/python.md:91) explicitly requires CPU-bound work to go to an executor. The bars route has the same pre-existing shape and the architecture frames the API as single-user, so it is not a merge blocker, but the new routes do stall every other request.

issues.title: TradeRecord.from_row maps trade values by position instead of by TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS.
issues.why: `from_row` reads `values[0..7]`. At head that order exactly matches `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS` (TRADE_COLUMNS minus market_ticker), so every field is assigned correctly today. The risk applies only if a future edit reorders TRADE_COLUMNS. That is maintainability hardening, not a current defect. It was later changed in daf30bec, and the regression test there needs a monkeypatched reorder to fail.

issues.title: tape_filtered re-implements the trades-filter membership test and hard-codes its parameter key, contrary to its docstring.
issues.why: `tape_filtered` reads `selection.params["trades_excluded_categories"]` and evaluates `(category or "") in bound`, which is a Python restatement of `COALESCE(s.category,'') = ANY(...)`. The docstring's claim that it is 'not re-spelled' is therefore inaccurate. The two forms agree today, and an integration test checks parity, so this is duplication and a misleading comment, not wrong behavior.

issues.title: Candle module docstring wrongly claims a new CANDLE_COLUMNS entry is served without an edit; models are hand-listed and _CANDLE_OBJECTS values are unused.
issues.why: `CandleBidAsk`/`CandlePrice` list their fields by hand, `from_row` hard-codes the object names and `volume_fp`/`open_interest_fp`, and only the keys of `_CANDLE_OBJECTS` are used. A new column would be dropped by pydantic's default `extra='ignore'` or would raise KeyError. Current output is correct, and a unit test catches mapping drift, so the defect is an overstated docstring plus a hypothetical future change.

issues.title: tape_complete_through is described as the newest stored trade's time but carries the trades sync watermark.
issues.why: `tape_facts` returns `sync_state['trades'].watermark_ts`, which `advance_watermark(window_edge)` sets and which slice 265 defines as explicitly NOT the newest stored trade. The value matches the 188 spec (slice line 302). Only the Field description and the `tape_facts` docstring are wrong. It is a published OpenAPI text error, not wrong data.

issues.title: tape_filtered description says no trades are stored for an excluded category, but previously stored trades are still served.
issues.why: `fetch_trades`/`count_trades` filter only on ticker and window, so any trades already stored for a category excluded later would still be returned while `tape_filtered` is true. This concerns the wording of a field description. Whether such rows actually exist depends on whether exclusion ever purges history, which I did not trace.

issues.title: _window uses the truthiness of a generic extra dict as the switch for a hard-coded period predicate.
issues.why: `_window` appends `period = %(period)s` when `extra` is truthy, and does not check that the key exists. The only callers are `_candle_window`, which always passes `{'period': period}`, and `_trade_window`, which passes nothing, so behavior is correct today. The concern is about an API shape that only a future caller could misuse.

issues.title: Count and fetch run as separate statements with separate snapshots, so the overage can exceed the 'one row' the docstring describes.
issues.why: The count and the fetch are separate statements on one connection with no REPEATABLE READ, so under READ COMMITTED a trades page committed in between can land in the response. The design accepts that the response may go over and is never truncated. The docstring's 'one row over' is illustrative wording, and the ceiling is a soft guard, so the effect is a slightly larger response and imprecise prose.

issues.title: The ceiling comparison is written twice per handler, once in _read and once in _admit_rows.
issues.why: Each handler checks `count > max_rows` inside the executor closure to skip the fetch, then calls `_admit_rows` with the same comparison to raise after the connection is released. This split is deliberate (the module docstring explains it), and the two checks agree today. It is a duplication point only.

issues.title: _admit_rows and _not_found are near-duplicates of the helpers in kalshi_catalog.py.
issues.why: The new `_admit_rows`/`_not_found` duplicate the catalog route's versions except for the remedy text. Behavior is correct. This is DRY cleanup, and it was later extracted to admission.py in daf30bec.

issues.title: The reversed-range 422 check and message are copied into windows.py rather than shared with bars.py.
issues.why: `resolve_window` re-spells the reversed-range check and message that `bars.py` already has for its date-typed bounds. Both behave correctly. The finding also mentions gaps.py's own window helpers, which are pre-existing (see 188-I13). The new part is a minor duplication.

issues.title: gaps.py still defines its own day-boundary window helpers instead of using windows.py.
issues.why: gaps.py is not touched in base..head; its `_window_start_utc`/`_window_end_utc` predate the slice (5b9bbcd5). Its end helper uses a different, documented half-open convention that is correct for its own predicate. Only the start helper is a true duplicate.

issues.title: The candle-ceiling load test asserts no latency or size bound and CANDLES_CEILING_RESPONSE_MB is never referenced.
issues.why: The candle test asserts only the row count, and the constant's docstring says it is 'recorded here rather than asserted' on purpose. The markets-list test checks correctness, not latency, and the module docstring's 'Four assertions' undercounts the six tests. These are test-quality points.

issues.title: The new load tier is not gated by CI.
issues.why: The tier is skipped unless MT_RUN_LOAD_TESTS=1, and the module docstring states that CI wiring belongs to slice 907. This is a documented, tracked process gap, not a code defect.

issues.title: The load test installs its recording cursor through the private pool._pool attribute and uses class-level mutable state.
issues.why: `_client` waits for the pool, sets the factory on a probe connection, and then walks `pool._pool` (noqa SLF001). `_RecordingCursor.statements` is class-level, and the test resets it before use. The no-fetch assertion is paired with `assert counts`, which limits vacuous passes. This is test brittleness, not a product defect.

issues.title: The concurrency load assertion uses the median, which cannot see the queued half of the requests.
issues.why: With 16 requests against a pool of 8, the median of 16 samples sits at the boundary between connected and queued requests, so a regression in queue wait could pass. This is true but concerns test sensitivity only.

issues.title: Docstrings say 'fourteen' candle value columns where CANDLE_COLUMNS has sixteen.
issues.why: `CandleRow` and the models module docstring say fourteen. The mapping has 14 nested columns plus `volume_fp` and `open_interest_fp`, and the code zips with strict=True, so it is correct. Only the prose is off.

issues.title: New test helpers and modules exceed the size guidance.
issues.why: `_seed_kalshi_dense` and the enlarged test modules are long, but this is a style guideline about size with no behavioral effect.
